title: File Inclusion and Path Traversal
learning_outcomes: Explain what file inclusion and path traversal contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: unsafe dynamic includes.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Security begins at trust boundaries. Validate data for the intended operation, encode output for its exact context, constrain file and network access, protect credentials, and apply authorization consistently. In this lesson, focus on unsafe dynamic includes; then compare it with local file inclusion. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use file inclusion and path traversal when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Security begins at trust boundaries. Validate data for the intended operation, encode output for its exact context, constrain file and network access, protect credentials, and apply authorization consistently. For file inclusion and path traversal, begin with unsafe dynamic includes. Also distinguish local file inclusion; remote file inclusion risks; canonicalizing and restricting paths. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for File Inclusion and Path Traversal
content_blocks.code:
<?php
$file = tempnam(sys_get_temp_dir(), "php-course-");
if ($file === false) { throw new RuntimeException("Cannot create temp file"); }
file_put_contents($file, "ready\n");
echo trim((string) file_get_contents($file)) . PHP_EOL;
unlink($file);

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Validate data at system boundaries and encode output for the target context; validation and escaping solve different problems.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating input validation as output escaping.
common_mistakes.why: A value can be valid data and still be unsafe in an HTML or JavaScript output context.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate shape and business rules at input boundaries, then apply context-appropriate output encoding.

common_mistakes.why: A request can be sent without the original form or browser UI.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat all security-relevant validation and authorization on the server.

common_mistakes.problem: Returning internal error details to the browser.
common_mistakes.why: Stack traces and configuration values may expose sensitive information.
common_mistakes.fix: Log safe diagnostics server-side and return a generic, useful response.
